title: L1A Concept
description: One concept ID from the tier blueprint. The content spine: every lesson, card, question, worksheet and media asset hangs off one of these. See docs/emt-blueprint.md 'Concept spec' and docs/master-plan.md 5, 6, 7, 10.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was authored against.

id.description: Concept ID: TIER-MM-LL-CC. Example EMT-02-03-04 = EMT tier, module 02 Airway, lesson 03 Oxygen delivery, concept 04 Non-rebreather mask.

title.description: Short human title, sentence case. Appears as the lesson heading and the card title.

domain.description: NREMT/exam domain tag, so exams can be weighted like the real thing. Preparatory, assessment and pharmacology concepts take whichever domain they feed. This enum is EMT-only and will be extended with the Fire (NFPA 1001 / Florida BFST) and Paramedic domain tags when those tiers begin.

difficulty.description: 1 = foundational, 3 = typical exam level, 5 = hardest application/scenario. Feeds question selection and SRS initial interval.

high_yield.description: Known exam favorite. Renders the Signal Yellow high-yield flag on cards and weights the concept up in focus drills.

prereqs.description: Concept IDs that should be complete before this one. Used to order lessons and to explain a locked item.

related.description: Concept IDs worth linking sideways to. Not gating; powers 'see also' and interleaved review.

pointer.description: A concept that is a signpost rather than a lesson. The value is an in-app hash route (for example "#/test"), and the screens render a link to it instead of pretending there is material here. Used by the Module 11 exam-prep placeholders.

key_points.description: The canonical facts. Every mode ends with this same Key Points box, and cards plus Teach It Back checks are generated from it. Keep each one atomic.

misconceptions.description: What learners get wrong, phrased as the wrong belief or the wrong action. Feeds distractor writing and Quiz It explanations.

exam_favorites.description: The angles this concept is actually tested from. Drives question_targets and the high-yield flag.

modes.description: The 8 learning modes. All optional so a concept can ship in Read + Quiz for Phase 1 and gain modes later; the app only renders the tabs that are present.

read.description: Mode 1 - Read. Layered textbook explanation. Plain English is the Phase 1 minimum; standard and deep unlock the depth toggle.

eli_new.description: Mode 2 - Explain Like I'm New. Analogy-first version for when the standard text bounces off.

analogy.description: The one-line hook, e.g. 'Preload is how full the balloon is before you squeeze it.'

see.description: Mode 3 - See It. Ordered list of media ids from this concept's media[] array: diagrams, labeled anatomy, flowcharts, algorithm trees, ECG strips, equipment photos.

hear.description: Mode 4 - Hear It. Default is browser text-to-speech over the script (decisions.md, Sept 15 2026); a pre-rendered file may override it.

script.description: What gets spoken. If omitted with source 'tts', the app narrates modes.read.standard, falling back to modes.read.plain.

audio.description: Media id of the audio asset. Required when source is 'file'.

do.description: Mode 5 - Do It. Names an interaction the app knows how to render and hands it this concept's data. Code never hardcodes the content.

activity.description: Stable slug for the interaction instance, e.g. 'select_device_scenario'.

type.description: Which renderer in js/ handles it.

config.description: Renderer-specific payload. Shape is owned by the matching module in js/.

quiz.description: Mode 6 - Quiz It. The lesson check. Questions live in the question bank and are pulled by concept ID; list ids here only to pin a specific set.

pool_size.description: How many questions to draw for the lesson check (master-plan 7: 5-10).

pass_pct.description: Lesson-complete threshold. 80 per the gating rules in master-plan 8.

teach.description: Mode 7 - Teach It Back. Learner explains it in their own words; the app checks the response against must_hit.

must_hit.description: Each entry is one idea the explanation has to contain, with the accepted wordings for a simple keyword match.

model_answer.description: Shown after the learner submits, never before.

story.description: Mode 8 - Story It. A short realistic call narrative from dispatch to handoff that carries the concept.

dispatch.description: The dispatch line that opens the narrative, e.g. 'Engine 1, Rescue 1 - 62-year-old male, difficulty breathing.'

cards.description: Which note-card types this concept generates for the curated deck and the SRS deck (master-plan 6).

card_data.description: Structured payload for the card types listed in cards[]. Every leaf is a string so nothing is silently coerced and printed wrong; the card renderer lays these out, it never parses prose. Include only the sub-object matching a type in cards[]. Values here are clinical content - fill them from a reviewed source, or leave the field out and set verify.

drug.description: Drug Card. EMT scope is assist/administer only - see docs/emt-blueprint.md module 09. Never write a dose that is not in the reviewed source; omit the field and set verify instead.

dose_adult.description: Adult dose exactly as the reviewed source words it, units included.

dose_peds.description: Pediatric dose exactly as the reviewed source words it, units included. Omit where no pediatric dose applies.

onset.description: Onset, and duration where the source gives it.

scope.description: Who may give it and how, e.g. which level administers versus assists. Renders as the scope flag on the card.

numbers.description: Numbers Card. Vitals ranges, scores, formulas, intervals. Rendered in the monospace face so figures line up.

label.description: What the figure is, e.g. the measurement and the population it applies to.

value.description: The figure or range as a string, so a range, an inequality or a formula all round-trip unchanged.

note.description: Caveat or condition attached to this figure.

skill.description: Skill Card. The numbered checklist, in order. Critical steps print in Signal Yellow - these are the ones that fail a station.

sheet.description: Which skill sheet this tracks, e.g. the NREMT or Florida station name.

critical.description: True = critical criterion. Missing it fails the station.

note.description: Common fail point or examiner cue.

mnemonic.description: Mnemonic Card. The acronym and what each letter stands for, in order.

expansion.description: One entry per letter, in acronym order.

memory_image.description: The picture to hang it on.

compare.description: Compare Card. Two easily-confused things side by side. Every row fills both sides so the columns stay parallel in print.

feature.description: What is being compared on this row, e.g. onset, or a given finding.

algorithm.description: Algorithm Card. A condensed decision tree. Nodes are the boxes, branches are the arrows between them; the renderer walks from the node named start.

start.description: Node id the tree begins at.

kind.description: decision = a question with branches out; action = do this; end = terminal.

condition.description: The arrow label - what makes you take this path.

question_targets.description: How many questions of each style the bank should hold for this concept. Blueprint budget is ~8 per concept to reach the 2,500-question EMT target.

media.description: Every asset this concept uses, in one place. Doubles as the copyright manifest required by master-plan 10.7 - nothing renders that is not listed here.

src.description: Path under media/, relative to the repo root.

alt.description: Required. Accessibility is a non-negotiable. Long is fine and often correct: a labelled anatomy diagram or an ECG strip needs every label spelled out, because alt text is the only way a screen-reader user gets the picture at all. Put the teaching point in caption instead - that is shown to everyone.

source.description: Where it came from. 'original' for assets drawn for L1A.

license.description: License or usage basis. Anything not clearly clean stays out.

print_safe.description: Whether it still reads in black and white on a printed card or worksheet.

labels.description: Optional. The structures this figure labels, each with a position so a generated worksheet can place a numbered pointer on the image instead of only asking for a list. Positions are percentages of the rendered image, measured from its top-left corner, so they survive any scaling — a figure used at 3in on a card and 6in on a worksheet needs no second set of coordinates. Point at the structure, not at the printed label: the worksheet hides the original labels and puts its own number there. Omit the array entirely for a figure with nothing to label, such as a flowchart whose boxes are the content.

id.description: Stable key for this label within the figure, lowercase snake_case. Worksheet answer keys reference it, so renaming one changes what a previously printed sheet means - prefer adding a new label to renaming an old one.

text.description: The answer: what the learner should write for this pointer.

x.description: Horizontal position as a percentage of image width, 0 at the left edge.

y.description: Vertical position as a percentage of image height, 0 at the top edge.

reviewed_against.description: Source text and guideline edition this concept was human-reviewed against, e.g. 'AAOS Emergency Care 12e / AHA 2025'. Not set = AI draft, not yet reviewed.

reviewed_on.description: Date of that review, ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Guidelines change; this is what makes a re-review sweep possible.

verify.description: True = something here is unconfirmed and must be checked against a source before it is trusted. Per CLAUDE.md, mark this rather than guessing, and never invent drug doses. The app shows a verify banner on the lesson and excludes the concept from module exams and full simulations. The same exclusion applies to any concept with no reviewed_against: module exams gate progression, so unreviewed or unverified content never decides whether a module is complete. Such concepts still appear in lessons, lesson checks, decks and focus drills.

verify_notes.description: What exactly needs checking, so the reviewer does not have to re-derive it. Expected whenever verify is true.

allOf.description: reviewed_against and reviewed_on travel together - a review date means nothing without the source.
If it is flagged for verification, say what needs verifying.

node_id.description: Algorithm node key, lowercase snake_case, unique within the card.
